title: Lines and Angles
description: Learn about parallel, perpendicular and intersecting lines for Class 4 Maths. Understand acute, right and obtuse angles with protractor use, real-life examples, 10 MCQs and 6 IMO questions.

topics.title: Types of Lines
topics.concept:
In geometry, a line is a straight path. In Grade 4, we study three important relationships between lines:

  • Parallel Lines: Lines that never meet and are always the same distance apart. Like railway tracks or opposite edges of a ruler.
  • Perpendicular Lines: Lines that meet at exactly 90 degrees (a right angle). Like the corner of a room or the letter L.
  • Intersecting Lines: Lines that cross each other at any angle. Like scissors or roads crossing at a junction.

A line segment has two endpoints. A ray has one endpoint and goes on forever in one direction.

examples.problem: Identify the type of lines formed by the two vertical bars in the letter 'H'.
examples.solution: The two vertical lines in 'H' are parallel — they run in the same direction, are always the same distance apart, and never meet.

examples.problem: Give two real-life examples each of parallel and perpendicular lines.
examples.solution: Parallel: railway tracks, opposite edges of a notebook. Perpendicular: corner of a wall meets the floor at 90 degrees; the letter 'L' shows perpendicular lines.

examples.problem: A road runs north-south. Another road crosses it going east-west. What type of lines do they form?
examples.solution: They form intersecting lines. If the crossing is at exactly 90 degrees, they are also perpendicular lines.

recap: Parallel lines: never meet, always same distance apart (like train tracks)
Perpendicular lines: meet at exactly 90 degrees (right angle)
Intersecting lines: cross each other at any angle
A line segment has two endpoints; a ray has one endpoint and goes on forever

topics.title: Types of Angles
topics.concept:
An angle is formed when two rays meet at a common point called the vertex. Angles are measured in degrees (°).

Three main types of angles:

  • Acute Angle: Less than 90 degrees (sharp, like the tip of a pencil)
  • Right Angle: Exactly 90 degrees (like the corner of a square)
  • Obtuse Angle: Between 90 and 180 degrees (wider than a right angle)

A straight angle = 180 degrees (a straight line).

examples.problem: Classify these angles: 45 degrees, 90 degrees, 135 degrees.
examples.solution: 45 degrees: Acute (less than 90). 90 degrees: Right angle (exactly 90). 135 degrees: Obtuse (between 90 and 180).

examples.problem: A clock shows 3:00. What type of angle do the hands make?
examples.solution: At 3:00, the minute hand points to 12 (top) and the hour hand points to 3 (right). The angle between them is exactly 90 degrees — a Right Angle.

examples.problem: If angle A = 35 degrees and angle B = 55 degrees share a common ray, what is the total angle formed?
examples.solution: Total angle = 35 + 55 = 90 degrees. This is a Right Angle.

recap: Acute angle: less than 90 degrees (looks sharp)
Right angle: exactly 90 degrees (looks like a square corner)
Obtuse angle: between 90 and 180 degrees (looks wide)
Two rays meeting at a vertex form an angle measured in degrees

topics.title: Using a Protractor to Measure Angles
topics.concept:
A protractor is the tool used to measure angles in degrees.

Steps to measure an angle with a protractor:

  • Place the centre hole of the protractor at the vertex of the angle
  • Align the baseline (0 line) with one ray of the angle
  • Read the degrees where the second ray crosses the scale
  • Use the scale that starts from 0 on the side where you placed the baseline

Protractors have two scales — always use the correct one!

examples.problem: Describe the steps to draw a 60 degree angle.
examples.solution: Step 1: Draw a ray. Step 2: Place protractor centre at the endpoint (vertex). Step 3: Align baseline with the ray. Step 4: Mark a point at 60 degrees on the scale. Step 5: Connect the vertex to that point with another ray.

examples.problem: A shape has 4 sides. All angles are 90 degrees. Opposite sides are parallel and equal. What shape is it?
examples.solution: A shape with 4 right angles, opposite sides parallel and equal is a Rectangle. If all four sides are also equal, it is a Square.

examples.problem: How many pairs of parallel lines does a rectangle have?
examples.solution: A rectangle has 2 pairs of parallel lines: the top and bottom sides are parallel, and the left and right sides are parallel.

recap: A protractor measures angles in degrees
Place centre hole at vertex, baseline along one ray, read where second ray points
Always use the scale that starts from 0 on the side of the first ray
Rectangles have 4 right angles (90 degrees) and 2 pairs of parallel sides

questions.explanation: Parallel lines always stay the same distance apart and never meet.
A right angle forms a perfect corner — exactly 90 degrees.

questions.q: Which shape has perpendicular lines (right angles)?
questions.explanation: Rectangles have 4 right angles (90 degree corners).

questions.q: An acute angle is ________ than 90 degrees.
questions.explanation: Acute means sharp — smaller than a right angle (less than 90 degrees).

questions.q: What tool is used to measure angles?
questions.explanation: A protractor has degree markings to measure angles accurately.

questions.q: Lines that cross each other at any angle are called?
questions.explanation: Intersecting lines cross each other at a point.

questions.q: The point where two rays meet to form an angle is called the:
questions.explanation: The vertex is the common point where two rays of an angle meet.
L has two lines meeting at exactly 90 degrees — a right angle.
Obtuse angles are wider than right angles (90) but less than straight angles (180).

questions.q: A clock shows 3:00. What type of angle do the hands make?
questions.explanation: At 3:00, hour hand at 3 and minute hand at 12 form exactly 90 degrees — a right angle.

questions.q: If two lines are perpendicular, what is the angle between them?
questions.explanation: Perpendicular means meeting at right angles — exactly 90 degrees.

questions.q: How many pairs of parallel lines does a rectangle have?
questions.explanation: Opposite sides are parallel — top/bottom form one pair, left/right form another. Total: 2 pairs.

questions.q: Angle A = 35 degrees and Angle B = 55 degrees share a common ray. The total angle formed is:
questions.explanation: Adjacent angles add up: 35 + 55 = 90 degrees — a right angle!

questions.q: Which statement about parallel lines is ALWAYS true?
questions.explanation: Parallel lines never meet, no matter how far they are extended.

questions.q: A shape has 4 sides. Opposite sides are parallel. ALL angles are 90 degrees. What could it be?
questions.explanation: Both squares and rectangles have 4 right angles and opposite sides parallel.

questions.q: If you fold a paper so one edge exactly lies on top of another edge, the fold line is ___ to both edges.
questions.explanation: The fold line (crease) meets both edges at exactly 90 degrees — it is perpendicular to both.
